dedupe_keys.name: bahia blanca argentina municipal solid waste collection routing and bin location instances

description: These benchmark files describe where household waste is generated along streets in an Argentine city, how long trucks take between collection points, and which bin sizes can be installed, so that routing and bin placement methods can be tested on real geography. The producers are Begoña González Landín and Máximo Méndez of the Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Diego Rossit of the Universidad Nacional del Sur and Mariano Frutos of CONICET, who used them in a 2025 Annals of Operations Research paper on combined periodic routing and bin location and a 2024 Urban Science paper on a scatter search method. Coverage is 19 instances from 12 to 163 collection points; the coordinates fall in Bahía Blanca, which this entry infers from the coordinates and the Universidad Nacional del Sur affiliation. Each instance lists points with daily waste volume, a travel time matrix in minutes, and a shared catalogue of bin combinations with capacity, service time and weekly cost. Both deposits are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: coordinates appear in longitude, latitude order despite the readme, and volumes are modelled, not weighed. Simulation uses: testing vehicle routing, collection frequency and bin location models for municipal waste. Related records: the Saltillo two-echelon instances (data-saltillo-waste-collection-2ecvrp-if-instances) offer a Mexican benchmark.
